Anyone knows how much cheaper it will be to launch a satellite using this plane vs the current system? Thanks!

On the order of $25M per launch. There's a number of projects underway all trying to crack the same problem: reusable launch vehicles. This is would be a complete game changer for space.

Consider commercial air travel as a parallel. Right now a trip from NY to LA is easy and affordable for most middle class people. Now imagine how much the airlines would have to charge if they had to remove the engines and refurbish the plane after each flight. That's what we're doing right now; throwing away a $20-25M launch vehicle and rebuilding it after each launch.

IMHO a carrier airframe is probably the best short term solution to the problem, but not the only one. SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Reactions Engine's Skylon are arguably better solutions, but more complex and harder to scale. I suspect that there's enough demand that they will all likely find a niche within the market.

Right now, we're talking about satellite launches, but ultimately payload is payload. Once the cost comes down affordable cargo to LEO is a key enabler to habitats and orbital build outs for Mars and the Jovian moons. This is what the space shuttle program was supposed to be before NASA screwed it up so badly. Cargo vans not Cadillacs. This is what gets us off this rock.
